model.title: Why is the Sahara a desert?

parts.text: It lies near the Tropic of Cancer
Air sinks there, so clouds rarely form
So it is a hot desert

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: Sinking air near the tropic gives very little rain

keywords.def: a large area with its own climate, plants and animals
tropical grassland with scattered trees and a wet and dry season
dense forest with heavy rain all year
an area with under 250 mm of rain a year and high temperatures
a long valley formed where the Earth's crust pulls apart

questions.q: Core: Label the Nile, Congo, Lake Victoria, Kilimanjaro, the Sahara and the Great Rift Valley on the map, and shade four biomes.
Stretch: Explain the band pattern of biomes north and south of the Equator.
questions.a: Rising air and rain at the Equator; sinking dry air near the tropics; bands mirror each other
B) Kilimanjaro. Kilimanjaro, in Tanzania, is 5,895 m; Everest is in Asia.
